question.problem:
For three random variables ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3},$ we have the following variances and covariances:

$$
\text{Var}[{X}_{1}]=2,\,\text{Var}[{X}_{2}]=5,\,\text{Var}[{X}_{3}]=3\,
$$

$$
\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]=4,\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{3}]=1,\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{2},{X}_{3}]=3\,
$$

Find $\text{Var}[{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}].$

current_example.problem:
For three random variables $X_1,X_2,$ and $X_3,$ we have the following variances and covariances:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X_1] = 1,   \qquad
\textrm{Var}[X_2] = 3,   \qquad
\textrm{Var}[X_3] = 8   \qquad
$$

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X_1,X_2] = 2,   \qquad
\textrm{Cov}[X_1,X_3] = 4,   \qquad
\textrm{Cov}[X_2,X_3] = -5   \qquad
$$

Find $\textrm{Var}[5X_1 + 2X_2 + 3X_3].$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ are random variables, and $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ are constants, then

$$
\textrm{Var}\left[\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} a_i X_i \right]
= \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} a_i^2 \textrm{Var}[X_i] + 2\sum\limits_{i <     j} a_i a_j \textrm{Cov}[X_i,X_j].
$$

Hence, for $n=3$ random variables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[{a}_{1}{X}_{1}+{a}_{2}{X}_{2}+{a}_{3}{X}_{3}] & ={a}_{1}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{1}]+{a}_{2}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{2}]+{a}_{3}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{3}] \\  & +2{a}_{1}{a}_{2}\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]+2{a}_{1}{a}_{3}\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{3}]+2{a}_{2}{a}_{3}\text{Cov}[{X}_{2},{X}_{3}].\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[5{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}+3{X}_{3}] & ={5}^{2}\cdot 1+{2}^{2}\cdot 3+{3}^{2}\cdot 8 \\  & +2\cdot 5\cdot 2\cdot 2+2\cdot 5\cdot 3\cdot 4+2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (-5) \\  & =25+12+72+40+120-60 \\  & =209.\end{aligned}
$$
